format_notice: Standalone review/experiment specification. Not an existing repository schema, executable test harness, game configuration, or source patch.
retrieval_note: Conversation/library searches recovered only the assignment; separate searches did not recover the referenced contract, queue, or checkpoint. This is not a claim that those files do not exist.
recommended_solution: Keep existing production mechanics and values. First map and measure the existing Steam exposure path; change at most one existing coefficient only if BAL-E1 accepts it. A passing baseline means no change.
principal_tradeoff: A narrow Steam pilot will not by itself resolve balance across all ten reactions or four delivery families.
strongest_counterargument: Steam may already be correct, or the actual problem may be accounting, stacking, geometry, or counterplay rather than its coefficient. In that case do not tune the coefficient.
source_needed: Ten reaction definitions and four projectile-family definitions
Authoritative payment, impact selection, allocation, interception, reaction consumption, Steam exposure/exit/overlap, and protection implementations plus relevant tests
unsupported_role_policy: Discard or hold any provisional role that conflicts with the current source; do not silently implement it as a contract change.

reactions.purpose: Broad Water preparation rather than concentrated finishing damage.
reactions.player_option: Seed an anticipated route for a later paid reaction instead of aiming only at the opponent.
reactions.counter: Rotate through untreated ground before committing to the prepared route.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Use Water as the setup ingredient for a later first-four pair, only where the actual registry permits retained ingredients.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Commit two Water contributions to preparation; spreading one finite output budget must not create a full-strength copy in each cell.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Repeated wetting or refreshing reissues the original quantity without new payment.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify actual Water retention, reaction output, lifetime, and refresh rules; a name alone does not establish these.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Chokepoint tempo control, conditional on existing movement-affecting behavior.
reactions.player_option: Place at a likely turn or landing point rather than covering an entire arena.
reactions.counter: Use an untreated alternate route; do not assume jumping grants immunity.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Water supplies one ingredient and Earth the other; time the second contribution when the route matters.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Spend two elements on position-dependent utility instead of immediate direct pressure.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Tiny repeat contributions renew a maximum movement penalty or create a station/spawn trap.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify any movement penalty, refresh rule, and airborne interaction; do not add them from this proposal.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Punish sustained occupation through accumulating scalding exposure, not concealment.
reactions.player_option: Force a choice between holding a useful position and leaving before exposure becomes costly.
reactions.counter: Leave affected cells promptly; recovery follows the existing exit/decay rule, which is not supplied.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine paid Water and Fire contributions at a chosen position; check real consumption before assuming leftovers remain.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Commit setup and Fire expenditure to dwell-time pressure rather than an immediate direct hit.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Boundary re-entry creates repeated entry damage, or overlapping fields charge the same exposure contribution twice.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify accumulation, damage conversion, merging/stacking, exit persistence, decay/reset, and protection rules.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Pressure an approach or escape route using the existing Water/Air behavior.
reactions.player_option: Prepare a flank rather than compete with Flood for stationary area coverage.
reactions.counter: Enter from an unprepared angle rather than follow the prepared route.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine Water setup with the actual Air interaction; no new movement boost, projectile redirection, or cleanse is implied.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Spend two ingredients on route utility; carrying or relocating an effect, if supported, cannot replenish its budget for free.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Relocation or cell traversal recreates full ingredient quantity or strength.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify what the current effect actually does; mobility, transport, and replenishment behavior are not documented here.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Defensive Earth positioning; cover is conditional on source-confirmed blocking geometry.
reactions.player_option: Split approach angles using existing blocking behavior, rather than seal every route.
reactions.counter: Flank the position; do not assume the effect is destructible.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Concentrate two Earth contributions at a useful defensive position.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Commit Earth resources to a location an opponent can choose not to contest.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Cheap indefinite refresh, impassable trap combinations, or denied station access.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify whether Rampart blocks movement/projectiles, its dimensions, lifetime, refresh, and legal placement.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Committed ground pressure, conditional on the actual hazard behavior.
reactions.player_option: Threaten a predicted landing or return route instead of chasing current position.
reactions.counter: Bait the placement and change route.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine Earth positioning and Fire expenditure through the existing recipe.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Trade two-element commitment for local pressure; do not assume a longer lifetime or higher damage than Steam without evidence.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Every selected cell receives the full output budget, or small additions renew a full-strength hazard.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify hazard, duration, output budget, allocation, and refresh semantics.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Earth/Air approach disruption through its existing effect.
reactions.player_option: Time pressure to an opponent crossing an exposed lane.
reactions.counter: Change approach angle or stagger entry rather than repeatedly contest the same lane.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine Earth and Air to support a follow-up shot; no blind, silence, or stagger is assumed.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Pay for a timing opportunity instead of guaranteed burst damage.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Each tiny Rapid/Spray contribution grants a full-strength control or reaction effect.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify actual utility and any per-hit or per-reaction minimum effect.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Concentrated Fire escalation using paid follow-up commitment.
reactions.player_option: Commit the second Fire contribution only when the opponent chooses to stay.
reactions.counter: Disengage before the follow-up expenditure is useful.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine two Fire contributions without assuming an extra multiplier or new stacking mechanic.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Spend additional Fire resources on a punish window rather than retain them for a later exchange.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Refresh increments output indefinitely or increases strength without consuming new ingredients.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify stacking, any amplification yield, lifetime, and finite output authorization.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Fire/Air pressure along a moving fight, without assuming the effect itself moves.
reactions.player_option: Lead an escape route instead of firing at the current location.
reactions.counter: Reverse or leave the threatened route laterally.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine Fire threat and the existing Air interaction.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Spatial reach, where supported, must be paid for or distribute a finite budget rather than duplicate it.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Spread, relocation, or repeated contact reissues an undiminished reaction budget.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify actual propagation/mobility, output allocation, and repeat-contact rules.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

reactions.purpose: Air-based positional control, conditional on source-confirmed force behavior.
reactions.player_option: Set a reversal or crossfire point using existing displacement behavior.
reactions.counter: Contest from outside the affected cells and another angle; do not assume an escape button or immunity.
reactions.base_element_synergy: Combine two Air contributions to support subsequent aimed pressure.
reactions.resource_tradeoff: Commit resources to control whose value depends on positioning and follow-up.
reactions.abuse_hypothesis: Repeated applications or several casters create an inescapable control loop.
reactions.mechanic_prerequisite: Verify any force, its integration, stacking, duration, and supported ways to leave; no new pull or hard control is proposed.
reactions.association_basis: Inferred from the parallel order of the pair and identity lists in S1; registry verification required.

experiments.name: Steam crossing versus holding
experiments.production_change: At most one existing Steam exposure-rate coefficient after source review and accepted results.
prerequisites: Pin the authoritative build and extract current Steam, payment, merge, exposure, reset/decay, and damage rules.
An existing independently adjustable exposure-rate coefficient must exist; otherwise BLOCKED, do not add one.
The legal baseline field must remain active for 240 ticks without free renewal; otherwise the planned long-dwell fixture is BLOCKED.
Use authoritative fixed-step inputs, the real whole-cell contact convention, and actual size templates.
placement_cases: outer affected-cell portion outside the selection circle when such a portion exists
measurements: Steam-attributed cumulative damage through natural status expiry
acceptance: For each size and placement, meet the median and p95 brief-crossing bounds and the sustained-exposure band.
More contact time must not reduce accumulated Steam-attributed damage when all other inputs match.

Re-entry must match the declared reset/decay semantics. In the absence of an explicitly paid entry bonus it must not exceed 1.05 times the continuous comparator. If comparator damage is zero, repeated-entry damage must also be zero; do not divide by zero.
No allocation, consumption, whole-cell, replay, or existing spawn-protection regressions.

Retain the baseline when it passes. Otherwise choose the passing coefficient closest to baseline; on an equal-distance tie select the one with less brief-crossing damage. If the tie persists, retain baseline pending evidence. If no candidate passes, make no change.
experiments.interpretation: These bands are untested tuning hypotheses, not evidence that the present Steam effect is wrong or that one coefficient is sufficient.

experiments.name: Equal-budget delivery-role comparison
prerequisites: Pin real costs, projectile parameters, legal cadence, paid strength/quantity, family definitions, and interception/recipe rules.
Use existing actor and target scripts through the real simulation.
fixed_controls: initial range within shared legal reach
aim policy within each role fixture
fixtures: single moving target and stationary precision control
broad ingredient preparation and recipe completion
measurement_rules: Stop legal casts before exceeding the gross mana cap; report unused mana and normalize outcomes by actual spending.
Do not manufacture fractional casts or free refills to equalize expenditure.
Record results at 600 ticks and also after already-paid outputs naturally finish; do not hide delayed Heavy impacts.
Use the minimum shared reachable range for matched-range comparisons, and a separate no-extrapolation range profile.
Reaction completion cost includes setup ingredients and failed or intercepted attempts.
acceptance: For a candidate role, its efficiency and price-of-specialization bounds must both hold in every size stratum on the paired-seed aggregate.
Do not divide by a zero Bolt comparator; mark that metric NOT_COMPARABLE and do not claim the role is validated.
Report all 12 paired outcomes and their range, not just a favorable average; these scripted comparisons do not establish population balance.
Reject a blanket buff when a family already wins all measured axes; propose no production changes without actual measurements.
Finite-strength and recipe-consumption checks remain mandatory; numeric role preferences never override current documented semantics.
experiments.interpretation: These inequalities test a proposed niche split. Failure falsifies that proposal, not necessarily the current game design.

experiments.name: Paid-budget fan-out and fragmentation
experiments.production_change: None without a reproducible, source-located accounting or refresh defect.
prerequisites: The existing resolver/harness must support equivalent paid input partitions and exact geometry fixtures without changing production mechanics.
Use the recipe-authorized finite output budget, including documented yields; never assume raw input damage equals reaction output strength.
Unsupported partition or cell counts are explicitly NOT_RUN, not simulated with a replacement resolver.
fixed_controls: same intended merged state for fragmentation-only comparisons
acceptance: Allocated child budgets do not exceed the recipe-authorized parent budget, within the declared arithmetic tolerance.
Reservation/consumption of each ingredient does not exceed that ingredient available to the resolver, including documented finite transformations.
Where the source contract requires the same authoritative merged state, require exact state/replay equivalence; the five-percent damage screen is not permission to violate exact semantics.
Where the contract intentionally gives different threshold or recipe outcomes, classify the difference rather than call it duplication.
No full-budget copy is created per packet, cell, refresh, or lineage restart.
Do not impose a global health-damage cap across multiple victims: multi-target damage and input-budget conservation are different quantities.
experiments.interpretation: This is a source-gated sensitivity and abuse experiment, not a proposed equal-split allocation formula or a new interception algorithm.

Other reactions and delivery-family values untouched
